title: Reading an indexed segment
statement: Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,N,p,\mathrm{top}$ be natural numbers, and let $l$ be a natural-number list of length $N$ whose entries agree with $\mu(a+i)$ for $0\le i<N$ (after viewing each entry as an integer), with every entry less than $p$ and $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. For every $i<N$, $\mu(a+i)$ equals the list entry at index $i$, using $0$ as the default when the index is out of range, viewed as an integer.
hypotheses_covered: Agreement of $l$ with $\mu$ on the segment starting at $a$
Every list entry is less than $p$
